questions.question: Why do images have a fixed token cost in multimodal models?
choices: Images are always the same file size
The vision encoder produces a standard number of tokens regardless of image complexity
Only small images have fixed token costs
questions.explanation: The vision encoder in multimodal models processes images into a fixed number of tokens (typically 1000 in simplified models), regardless of whether the image is a simple icon or a complex photograph.

questions.question: What is the correct way to estimate text tokens?
choices: Divide content length by ~4 (characters per token)
Use a fixed 100 tokens per text block
questions.explanation: Text tokens in most models average about 4 characters per token. So a 200-character text block is roughly 50 tokens (200 / 4 = 50).

questions.question: Why should you return a consistent structure even when there's no input?
choices: Callers expect a consistent shape and may crash on undefined properties
Empty input is impossible in production
questions.explanation: If the caller expects `{ textParts: [], imageRefs: [], combined: '', tokens: 0 }` and instead gets `undefined` or `null`, accessing `.length` or other properties will throw errors. A consistent shape prevents runtime crashes.
